subject: Life Skills
title: Warren Buffett's Two-List Strategy
description: Learn Warren Buffett's Two-List Strategy in one minute.

hook.text: Buffett asked his pilot to write 25 career goals. Then he told him to circle only the top five.

buildup.text: The pilot assumed the remaining 20 were a secondary list to work on occasionally during slower times.

discovery.text: Buffett said the opposite: those 20 become your 'avoid at all costs' list. They are the dangerous distractions.

twist.text: The real enemies of focus are not bad ideas. They are good ideas that are not great. They seduce and scatter you.

climax.text: Saying no to mediocre goals is harder than saying no to bad ones. But it is the only path to exceptional results.

punchline.text: Good is the enemy of great. Cut the 20.

quiz.question: What did Buffett say about the 20 goals not in the top five?
options: Work on them whenever you have free time
Avoid them at all costs — they are dangerous distractions
